deck_title: Green-Cauchy rotation-invariant finite strain vs naive linearized strain ghost bloat rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic George Green (1841) & Barre de Saint-Venant (1845) quadratic finite strain tensor (E_Green = 0.5*(F^T F - I), where orthogonal rotation cancels identically via R^T R = I so rest-state equilibrium stretch ratio locks at lambda = 1.0000x across all 17 rigid-rotation stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with cos(theta) = 1/(1+u) and 0/17 bloated stations) versus naive infinitesimal linearized Cauchy strain (eps_lin = 0.5*(F + F^T) - I = (lambda*cos(theta) - 1)*I, which mistakes rigid rotation for compression and expands equilibrium edge length as lambda = 1/cos(theta) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at theta=60 deg u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-substep incremental corotational integration.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Large-deformation FEM soft bodies, elastic characters, cloth bending, and vegetation swaying through arbitrary 3D rotations
St. Venant-Kirchhoff, Neo-Hookean, and XPBD finite-strain continuum solvers requiring exact SO(3) objectivity
Eliminating the 1/cos(theta) linear-FEM ghost inflation artifact when appendages rotate past 30-60 degrees
Zero-SVD quadratic strain energy evaluation via C = F^T * F
not_for: Purely static bridges or buildings with sub-milliradian rotations where infinitesimal strain is valid
Unconstrained point-cloud particles without elastic connectivity

dark_box.lead: MIT original code. Synthetic educational scene; local checks reproduced. No production, physics, or neural inference certification.
